sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)
savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.type: tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner itaretara-dvandva, whose second member is a nañ-tatpuruṣa)
samasa.vigraha: न दक्षिणाः अदक्षिणाः; दक्षिणाः च अदक्षिणाः च दक्षिणादक्षिणाः; दक्षिणादक्षिणैः आराध्या दक्षिणादक्षिणाराध्या
samasa.vigraha_iast: na dakṣiṇāḥ adakṣiṇāḥ; dakṣiṇāḥ ca adakṣiṇāḥ ca dakṣiṇādakṣiṇāḥ; dakṣiṇādakṣiṇaiḥ ārādhyā dakṣiṇādakṣiṇārādhyā
samasa.explanation: (1) a-dakṣiṇa 'not of the right' (nañ-tatpuruṣa). (2) dakṣiṇa and adakṣiṇa are joined as a dvandva, 'those of the right and those not of the right'. (3) The gerundive ārādhyā 'to be worshipped' is the head and takes the dvandva in the instrumental of the agent: 'to be worshipped by both'. The long ā after the first dakṣiṇa hides the negative a- of the second member, which is why the name is easily misread as dakṣiṇā + dakṣiṇa.

components.meaning: right; of the right-hand (dakṣiṇa) way of worship; also skillful, learned
not of the right: of the left-hand (vāma) way; also unskilled, simple
to be worshipped, to be propitiated

names.meaning: She who is worshipped by those of the right-hand path and those of the left
names.significance: Traditionally dakṣiṇa and adakṣiṇa are the right-hand (Vedic, samaya) and left-hand (vāma) modes of worship, and She receives both; the pair is also read as the learned and the unlearned, both of whom reach Her.

meaning_check.note: Tidied ('right-hand and left-hand'); the meaning follows the dvandva dakṣiṇa + adakṣiṇa.

names.previous_split_issues: The negative a- of adakṣiṇa was lost: the name was split as dakṣiṇā + dakṣiṇārādhyā ('worshipped by the right-hand path'), dropping the left-hand worshipers and the dvandva.
names.uncertain: Besides right-hand / left-hand ways, the pair is also read as the skillful and the unskillful (learned and unlearned); both readings rest on the same dvandva.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (over an inner karmadhāraya and an upamita-karmadhāraya)
samasa.vigraha: दरम् स्मेरम् दरस्मेरम्; मुखम् अम्बुजम् इव मुखाम्बुजम्; दरस्मेरम् मुखाम्बुजम् यस्याः सा दरस्मेरमुखाम्बुजा
samasa.vigraha_iast: daram smeram darasmeram; mukham ambujam iva mukhāmbujam; darasmeram mukhāmbujam yasyāḥ sā darasmeramukhāmbujā
samasa.explanation: (1) dara-smera 'slightly smiling': the indeclinable dara 'a little' qualifies smera 'smiling'. (2) mukha-ambuja 'the face that is like a lotus': an upamita compound, the face compared to the lotus with the comparison word iva understood. (3) (1) qualifies (2), and the whole is a bahuvrīhi describing Her: 'She whose lotus-face is gently smiling'; ambuja takes the feminine -ā.

components.note: ambu 'water' + ja 'born'; with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She whose lotus-face wears a gentle smile
names.significance: The slight smile is traditionally read as the outward sign of Her grace: it reassures the devotee and, in the Purāṇic account, is enough to destroy the demons.

meaning_check.note: dara means 'slightly', so the smile is gentle rather than 'sweet'.

names.previous_split_issues: mukhāmbujā was left as one row ('lotus-faced'); it is mukha 'face' + ambuja 'lotus', joined by savarṇa-dīrgha.

samasa.type: karmadhāraya (one name made of two co-referential words); a tatpuruṣa reading is also given
samasa.vigraha: कौलिनी च असौ केवला च कौलिनीकेवला; अथवा कौलिनीनाम् केवला कौलिनीकेवला
samasa.vigraha_iast: kaulinī ca asau kevalā ca kaulinīkevalā; athavā kaulinīnām kevalā kaulinīkevalā
samasa.explanation: Read as one name, kaulinī 'She of the Kula (the Kaula tradition)' and kevalā 'the Absolute, unmixed, alone' stand in apposition: 'the Kaula Goddess who is the Absolute'. A genitive reading, 'the Absolute for the Kaulas', underlies the traditional gloss that the followers of the Kaula way worship Her as pure consciousness. The words meet without sound change.

components.meaning: She of the Kula; the Goddess of the Kaula tradition
components.note: kaula 'pertaining to the kula' + the possessive -in, feminine -ī

components.meaning: alone, absolute, unmixed; pure consciousness without a second

names.meaning: She who, for the followers of the Kaula way, is the Absolute, pure consciousness
names.significance: Kula is the whole of manifest reality held together in Śakti; for the Kaula practitioner the Goddess of the Kula is herself kevala, the one consciousness without a second.

meaning_check.note: Tidied: 'Kaula' put into IAST; 'worshipped as' recast so the sentence follows the compound.

names.previous_split_issues: No word-split was given (the name was written as two words); kaulinī + kevalā added.
names.uncertain: The internal relation (apposition, or a genitive 'the Absolute for the Kaulas') is not settled; both are traditional and the meaning combines them.
names.variants: Some printings write कौलिनी केवला as two words; the 1,000-name count requires one name here (see the correction log).

samasa.type: upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya, itself over a nañ-tatpuruṣa and a karmadhāraya)
samasa.vigraha: न अर्घ्यम् अनर्घ्यम्; कैवल्यम् एव पदम् कैवल्यपदम्; अनर्घ्यम् कैवल्यपदम् अनर्घ्यकैवल्यपदम्; अनर्घ्यकैवल्यपदम् ददाति इति अनर्घ्यकैवल्यपददायिनी
samasa.vigraha_iast: na arghyam anarghyam; kaivalyam eva padam kaivalyapadam; anarghyam kaivalyapadam anarghyakaivalyapadam; anarghyakaivalyapadam dadāti iti anarghyakaivalyapadadāyinī
samasa.explanation: (1) an-arghya 'beyond price' (nañ-tatpuruṣa; na becomes an- before a vowel). (2) kaivalya-pada 'the state that is kaivalya' (karmadhāraya of identity). (3) (1) qualifies (2). (4) dāyinī 'giver' is the head and takes (3) as its object: 'She who gives the priceless state of liberation'.

components.note: nañ (a-, an- before a vowel) + arghya 'to be valued'

names.meaning: She who bestows the priceless state of final liberation (kaivalya)
names.significance: Kaivalya, the isolation of the Self from all that is not the Self, is the highest goal; nothing can be paid for it, so it is Her gift alone.

meaning_check.note: 'fruit' is not in the name; pada is the state or abode of kaivalya.

names.previous_split_issues: pada was glossed 'foot'; here it is 'state, station'.

samasa.explanation: stotra 'hymns' and priya 'dear' are co-referential and the compound describes Her: 'She to whom hymns are dear'. priya takes the feminine -ā.

names.meaning: She who is fond of hymns in Her praise
names.significance: Traditionally the name assures the reciter that the hymn itself, this Sahasranāma included, is an offering She loves.

names.meaning: She who is rich in praise, the true object of all praises
names.significance: Every hymn, wherever it is addressed, finally reaches Her; so all praise is Hers.

meaning_check.note: -matī 'possessing' made explicit; 'essence' dropped as it is not in the name.

names.previous_split_issues: matī was glossed 'minded', as if it were mati 'mind'; it is the possessive suffix -mat (stuti-mat 'possessed of praise').

sandhi.rule: the final m of the prefix sam becomes anusvāra before a consonant (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ)

samasa.vigraha: श्रुतिभिः संस्तुतम् श्रुतिसंस्तुतम्; श्रुतिसंस्तुतम् वैभवम् यस्याः सा श्रुतिसंस्तुतवैभवा
samasa.vigraha_iast: śrutibhiḥ saṃstutam śrutisaṃstutam; śrutisaṃstutam vaibhavam yasyāḥ sā śrutisaṃstutavaibhavā
samasa.explanation: (1) śruti-saṃstuta 'well praised by the Śrutis' (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa; the participle is the head, the Vedas its agents). (2) This qualifies vaibhava 'glory', and the whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose glory is extolled by the Śrutis'; vaibhava takes the feminine -ā.

components.note: vaibhava (from vibhu 'all-pervading'), with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She whose glory is extolled by the Śrutis (the Vedas)
names.significance: The Upaniṣads praise Her greatness as the supreme Brahman even where they do not name Her.

meaning_check.note: 'Śrutis' put into IAST and glossed.

components.note: keeps its s before the possessive -vin (Pāṇini 1.4.19 tasau matvarthe)

names.meaning: She who is high-minded, of strong and independent mind
names.significance: Traditionally: Her mind depends on nothing outside Herself; She is self-determined and steadfast.

meaning_check.note: 'well-known for Her mind' missed the sense of -vin (possessing a mind in a high degree: wise, resolute, high-minded).

components.meaning: honor, dignity, self-respect; also the proud indignation of a beloved

components.note: the possessive suffix -mat, which becomes -vat after a stem in a (Pāṇini 8.2.9), feminine -ī

names.meaning: She who is high-minded, full of dignity and honor
names.significance: Traditionally māna is also the proud indignation of love, so the name recalls Her loving pride toward Kāmeśvara; She is also the one honored by all.

meaning_check.note: māna is dignity and honor; 'great fame' narrowed to 'honor'.

sandhi.rule: guṇa: ā + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

samasa.type: karmadhāraya (maheśa), with the feminine of association; or karmadhāraya on the feminine directly
samasa.vigraha: महान् ईशः महेशः; महेशस्य पत्नी महेशी; अथवा महती ईशी महेशी
samasa.vigraha_iast: mahān īśaḥ maheśaḥ; maheśasya patnī maheśī; athavā mahatī īśī maheśī
samasa.explanation: Two analyses give the same form. (1) mahā-īśa 'the great Lord', Maheśa (Śiva), whose wife is called Maheśī by the feminine of association. (2) mahatī īśī 'the great sovereign Lady' directly, mahatī becoming mahā- in a karmadhāraya (Pāṇini 6.3.42, 6.3.46).

components.note: appears as mahā- in a karmadhāraya (Pāṇini 6.3.46)

names.meaning: She who is the consort of Maheśa (Śiva), the great sovereign Goddess
names.significance: As Maheśī She is Śiva's own power, inseparable from Maheśvara; in Her own right She is the supreme ruler.

meaning_check.note: 'mahesha (shiva)' put into IAST; the second analysis ('great sovereign') added.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.explanation: maṅgala 'auspicious' qualifies ākṛti 'form' and the whole describes Her: 'She whose form is auspicious'. ākṛti is already feminine and keeps its ending; the adjective stands in its basic stem maṅgala.

names.meaning: She who is of auspicious form
names.significance: To see or meditate on Her form is itself auspicious; whatever is auspicious in the world is a reflection of Her.

samasa.explanation: mātā 'mother' is the head; viśva 'the universe' stands to it in the genitive: 'the Mother of the universe'.

names.meaning: She who is the Mother of the universe
names.significance: She brings forth the universe and cares for it as a mother cares for her child.

meaning_check.note: Capitalization tidied.

sandhi.rule: jaśtva: a final t becomes d before a voiced sound (Pāṇini 8.2.39 jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte)

samasa.explanation: dhātrī 'nurse, supporter' is the head; jagat 'the world' stands to it in the genitive: 'the nurse and sustainer of the world'.

components.note: stem jagat; d only by jaśtva before dh

names.meaning: She who is the nurse and sustainer of the world
names.significance: After name 934 has called Her Mother, this name calls Her the nurse who feeds and protects what She has brought forth.

meaning_check.note: dhātrī is both 'nurse' and 'sustainer'; 'mother who protects' tightened.

names.previous_split_issues: jagad was given in its sandhi form; the stem is jagat (d only by jaśtva before dhātrī).

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.explanation: viśāla 'wide, large' qualifies akṣi 'eye', and the whole describes Her: 'She whose eyes are large'. At the end of a bahuvrīhi akṣi becomes akṣa (Pāṇini 5.4.113 bahuvrīhau sakthyakṣṇoḥ svāṅgāt ṣac), and the feminine is akṣī.

components.note: akṣi, as akṣa at the end of a bahuvrīhi, with the feminine -ī

names.meaning: She who has large eyes
names.significance: Wide eyes are a classical mark of beauty and also of the all-seeing; Viśālākṣī is the name under which the Goddess is worshipped at Kāśī.

components.note: the possessive suffix -in, feminine -ī; n becomes ṇ after the r

names.meaning: She who is dispassionate
names.significance: Though She enjoys the play of the worlds, nothing in them binds Her; She is the model of the vairāgya the seeker must cultivate.

names.meaning: She who is skillful and confident
names.significance: Traditionally: She is accomplished in every art and acts with complete assurance in creating and governing the worlds.

sandhi.rule: guṇa: a + u → o (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

samasa.explanation: parama 'supreme' qualifies udārā 'generous, noble' (both refer to Her; parama takes its masculine stem by puṃvadbhāva): 'supremely generous'.

names.meaning: She who is supremely generous
names.significance: Her generosity has no limit: She gives even Herself to the devotee.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.explanation: para 'supreme' qualifies āmoda 'joy, delight', and the whole describes Her: 'She whose joy is supreme'; āmoda takes the feminine -ā. The string could also be cut parā + modā (moda 'joy'), with the same sense.

components.note: āmoda, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She who is supremely joyful
names.significance: Her joy is the bliss (ānanda) that is Her very nature, not a joy dependent on anything; āmoda also means fragrance, the 'scent' of that bliss. With 939 it plays on the same syllables: param-odārā, parām-odā.
names.uncertain: The usual division is para + āmodā; parā + modā is also possible, with the same sense.

sandhi.rule: the final s of manas becomes u after a and before a voiced consonant, and a + u → o (Pāṇini 6.1.114 haśi ca, with 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

names.meaning: She who is in the form of the mind
names.significance: In the Taittirīya Upaniṣad the manomaya kośa is the sheath made of mind; She pervades it and is also the power by which the mind thinks.
names.previous_split_issues: mano was given in its sandhi form; the stem is manas (o by sandhi before -maya), and -mayī is a suffix, 'consisting of'.

samasa.explanation: vyoman 'sky' is identified with keśa 'hair' (the sky is Her hair), and the whole describes Her; keśa, a body part, takes the feminine -ī (Pāṇini 4.1.54). vyoman drops its final n in the compound.

components.note: appears as vyoma- (final n dropped, Pāṇini 8.2.7 nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya)
keśa, with the feminine -ī of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She who has the sky as Her hair
names.significance: Her cosmic form fills space, its tresses being the sky. Vyomakeśa is also a name of Śiva, so the name is read as well as 'consort of Vyomakeśa'.

samasa.explanation: -sthā 'standing, abiding' (√sthā with the suffix -a, Pāṇini 3.2.4 supi sthaḥ) is the head and takes vimāna in the locative: 'abiding in the celestial car'.

components.meaning: celestial car or palace; also the towered shrine of a temple

names.meaning: She who is seated in Her celestial chariot
names.significance: Traditionally She is enthroned in Her aerial car, travelling with the gods; vimāna is also the temple tower over the sanctum, where She dwells as the presiding deity.

meaning_check.note: The second gloss ('journeys … with the gods') is interpretation, moved to significance.

components.note: the possessive suffix -in, feminine -ī; n becomes ṇ after the r

names.meaning: She who bears the thunderbolt (vajra)
names.significance: Traditionally read also as Indrāṇī, the power of Indra the vajra-bearer (vajrin), and as 'She who is adorned with diamonds'.

meaning_check.note: 'vajrA' put into IAST.

sandhi.rule: guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa; as a name, the feminine of Vāmakeśvara
samasa.vigraha: वामकस्य ईश्वरी वामकेश्वरी; अथवा वामकेश्वरस्य पत्नी वामकेश्वरी
samasa.vigraha_iast: vāmakasya īśvarī vāmakeśvarī; athavā vāmakeśvarasya patnī vāmakeśvarī
samasa.explanation: Vāmakeśvara, 'the Lord of the vāmaka', is a name of Śiva; Vāmakeśvarī is his consort, or directly 'the Sovereign of the vāmaka'. īśvarī is the head. The name also recalls the Vāmakeśvara Tantra, a root text of Śrīvidyā.

components.meaning: vāmaka: 'the left' or 'the beautiful'; the vāma way

names.meaning: She who is Vāmakeśvarī, the sovereign Goddess of the Vāmakeśvara Tantra
names.significance: The Vāmakeśvara Tantra (with the Nityāṣoḍaśikārṇava) is a foundational text of Śrīvidyā, and She is its presiding deity, the consort of Vāmakeśvara (Śiva).

meaning_check.note: 'vamakeshvara tantra' put into IAST; the name itself (Vāmakeśvarī) stated, as the Tantra is named after Her consort.

names.uncertain: The sense of vāmaka (the left-hand way, or 'beauty') is variously explained.

samasa.vigraha: पञ्च यज्ञाः पञ्चयज्ञाः; पञ्चयज्ञाः प्रियाः यस्याः सा पञ्चयज्ञप्रिया
samasa.vigraha_iast: pañca yajñāḥ pañcayajñāḥ; pañcayajñāḥ priyāḥ yasyāḥ sā pañcayajñapriyā
samasa.explanation: (1) pañca-yajña 'the five sacrifices': a numeral compound (dvigu), formed because another member follows (Pāṇini 2.1.51). (2) priyā 'dear' is co-referential, and the whole describes Her: 'She to whom the five sacrifices are dear'.

components.note: appears as pañca- (final n dropped, Pāṇini 8.2.7)

names.meaning: She who is fond of the five forms of sacrifice
names.significance: The five are traditionally the śrauta rites agnihotra, darśapūrṇamāsa, cāturmāsya, paśu (animal) and soma sacrifices; they are also read as the five daily mahāyajñas (to the gods, sages, ancestors, beings and humans).

meaning_check.note: The list of five, given in ITRANS, moved to significance and put into IAST; its 'goyajña' does not match the usual list (paśu sacrifice).

names.uncertain: Which five sacrifices are meant (śrauta rites, the five mahāyajñas, or Āgamic five) differs between explanations.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: पञ्च प्रेताः पञ्चप्रेताः; पञ्चप्रेतानाम् मञ्चः पञ्चप्रेतमञ्चः; पञ्चप्रेतमञ्चम् अधिशेते इति पञ्चप्रेतमञ्चाधिशायिनी
samasa.vigraha_iast: pañca pretāḥ pañcapretāḥ; pañcapretānām mañcaḥ pañcapretamañcaḥ; pañcapretamañcam adhiśete iti pañcapretamañcādhiśāyinī
samasa.explanation: (1) pañca-preta 'the five corpses' (dvigu). (2) pañcapreta-mañca 'the couch of (made of) the five corpses' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) adhiśāyinī 'reclining upon' is the head and takes the couch as its object: with adhi, √śī governs the accusative of the place (Pāṇini 1.4.46 adhiśīṅsthāsāṃ karma).

names.meaning: She who reclines on a couch made of the five corpses
names.significance: The five are Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, Īśvara and Sadāśiva: four form the legs and Sadāśiva the plank. Without Her power even these gods are lifeless (preta); compare name 249, pañcapretāsanāsīnā.
names.previous_split_issues: mañcādhiśāyinī was left as one row ('reclining on a throne of'); it is mañca 'couch' + adhiśāyinī 'reclining upon', joined by savarṇa-dīrgha.

names.meaning: She who is the fifth, beyond Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra and Īśvara
names.significance: Traditionally She is the power of Sadāśiva, the fifth beyond the four gods of creation, maintenance, dissolution and veiling; Pañcamī is also one of the twelve names of Vārāhī, Her commander.

meaning_check.note: 'brahmA, viShNu, rudra and Ishvara' put into IAST.

sandhi.rule: guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: पञ्च भूतानि पञ्चभूतानि; पञ्चभूतानाम् ईशी पञ्चभूतेशी
samasa.vigraha_iast: pañca bhūtāni pañcabhūtāni; pañcabhūtānām īśī pañcabhūteśī
samasa.explanation: (1) pañca-bhūta 'the five elements' (dvigu). (2) īśī 'sovereign lady' is the head and the elements stand to it in the genitive: 'the sovereign of the five elements'.

names.meaning: She who is the sovereign of the five elements
names.significance: Earth, water, fire, air and space arise from Her and obey Her; inwardly the five elements are mastered in the five lower cakras, which She rules.
names.previous_split_issues: bhūteśī was left as one row ('ruler of elements'); it is bhūta + īśī, joined by guṇa.

sandhi.rule: the final m of the prefix sam becomes anusvāra and then the nasal of the following k-row, ṅ (Pāṇini 8.3.23, 8.4.59)
guṇa: ā + u → o (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (over an inner bahuvrīhi), completed by the possessive suffix -in
samasa.vigraha: पञ्च सङ्ख्या येषाम् ते पञ्चसङ्ख्याः; पञ्चसङ्ख्याः उपचाराः पञ्चसङ्ख्योपचाराः; पञ्चसङ्ख्योपचाराः अस्याः सन्ति इति पञ्चसङ्ख्योपचारिणी
samasa.vigraha_iast: pañca saṅkhyā yeṣām te pañcasaṅkhyāḥ; pañcasaṅkhyāḥ upacārāḥ pañcasaṅkhyopacārāḥ; pañcasaṅkhyopacārāḥ asyāḥ santi iti pañcasaṅkhyopacāriṇī
samasa.explanation: (1) pañca-saṅkhya 'whose number is five' (bahuvrīhi), qualifying (2) upacāra 'service, offering of worship'. (3) The possessive -in (feminine -iṇī) makes the whole describe Her: 'She who has (receives) the services numbering five'.

components.note: the possessive suffix -in, feminine -ī; n becomes ṇ after the r

names.meaning: She who is worshipped with the fivefold offerings (fragrance, flowers, incense, lamp and food)
names.significance: The pañcopacāra pūjā, the simplest complete worship, offers gandha, puṣpa, dhūpa, dīpa and naivedya; traditionally these also stand for the five elements offered back to Her.

meaning_check.note: Wording tightened; the five offerings given with their worship names in significance.

names.previous_split_issues: saṅkhyopacāriṇī was left as one row; it is saṅkhyā 'number' + upacāra 'offering' + the possessive -in.

names.meaning: She who is eternal
names.significance: Everything with a beginning has an end; She alone has neither.

sandhi.rule: vṛddhi: a + ai → ai (Pāṇini 6.1.88 vṛddhir eci)

samasa.explanation: śāśvata 'eternal' qualifies aiśvarya 'sovereignty', and the whole describes Her: 'She whose sovereignty is eternal'; aiśvarya takes the feminine -ā.

components.note: aiśvarya (abstract noun from īśvara), with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She who holds eternal sovereignty
names.significance: Her rule over the worlds is not acquired and cannot be lost; the powers (aiśvarya) sought by others are Hers by nature.

samasa.explanation: -dā 'giving' (√dā with the suffix -a, Pāṇini 3.2.3 āto 'nupasarge kaḥ) is the head and takes śarman as its object: 'giver of happiness'.

names.meaning: She who is the giver of happiness
names.significance: Śarman is both happiness and refuge: She gives the lasting well-being that comes from shelter in Her.

samasa.explanation: mohinī 'enchantress' (causative of √muh with -in) is the head and takes Śambhu as its object: 'She who enchants Śambhu'.

names.meaning: She who enchants Śambhu (Śiva)
names.significance: Śiva, absorbed in himself, is drawn by Her beauty into union with Her, and from that union creation proceeds.

meaning_check.note: 'deludes' sharpened to 'enchants', and Śiva put into IAST.

sandhi.rule: no sound change: a name boundary, not a sandhi. Bhāskararāya divides the verse's धराधरसुता into two names, dharā (955) and dharasutā (956); read as one word, dharādhara-sutā, it would be a single name 'daughter of the mountain', and the count of 1,000 needs two

names.meaning: She who is the Earth, the bearer of all
names.significance: As the earth bears all beings patiently, She bears the whole universe.

meaning_check.note: 'mother earth' kept in sense; dharā 'bearer' rendered.

sandhi.rule: no sound change: a name boundary, not a sandhi. Bhāskararāya divides the verse's धराधरसुता into two names, dharā (955) and dharasutā (956); read as one word, dharādhara-sutā, it would be a single name 'daughter of the mountain', and the count of 1,000 needs two

samasa.explanation: sutā 'daughter' is the head; dhara 'the mountain' stands to it in the genitive: 'the daughter of the mountain', Pārvatī, daughter of Himavat.

names.meaning: She who is the daughter of the mountain (Himavat)
names.significance: As Pārvatī She is born as the daughter of Himavat, king of mountains, to become Śiva's bride.

meaning_check.note: 'dhara (himavat)' put into IAST.

names.meaning: She who possesses great wealth; She who is supremely blessed
names.significance: Every kind of fortune is Hers, and those who worship Her become blessed (dhanya) too.

meaning_check.note: Typo 'possessses' corrected.

components.meaning: dharma: righteousness, the order that sustains

components.note: the possessive suffix -in, feminine -ī; n becomes ṇ after the r

names.meaning: She who is righteous
names.significance: Dharma is Her own nature; She is also the one who upholds it in the world.

samasa.explanation: vardhinī 'increaser' (causative of √vṛdh with -in) is the head and takes dharma as its object: 'She who makes dharma grow'.

names.meaning: She who promotes righteousness
names.significance: She strengthens dharma in the world and in the life of the devotee.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.explanation: The participle atītā 'gone beyond' is the head and takes the first member as its object in the accusative; atīta is one of the words that form such compounds (Pāṇini 2.1.24 dvitīyā śrita-atīta-patita-gata-atyasta-prāpta-āpannaiḥ).

names.meaning: She who transcends the worlds
names.significance: She pervades all the worlds and yet is not contained by them.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.explanation: The participle atītā 'gone beyond' is the head and takes the first member as its object in the accusative; atīta is one of the words that form such compounds (Pāṇini 2.1.24 dvitīyā śrita-atīta-patita-gata-atyasta-prāpta-āpannaiḥ).

components.meaning: the guṇas: sattva, rajas and tamas

names.meaning: She who transcends the guṇas
names.significance: As nirguṇa Brahman She stands beyond sattva, rajas and tamas, though She wields them in creation (name 984).

meaning_check.note: 'guNAs' put into IAST.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.explanation: The participle atītā 'gone beyond' is the head and takes the first member as its object in the accusative; atīta is one of the words that form such compounds (Pāṇini 2.1.24 dvitīyā śrita-atīta-patita-gata-atyasta-prāpta-āpannaiḥ).

names.meaning: She who transcends everything
names.significance: The three names 960–962 widen step by step: beyond the worlds, beyond the qualities that make them, beyond all that is.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.explanation: śama 'tranquility' is identified with ātman 'self, nature', and the whole describes Her: 'She whose very nature is tranquility'. The bahuvrīhi takes the suffix -ka, whose a becomes i before the feminine -ā (ātmikā).

names.meaning: She whose very nature is tranquility
names.significance: Śama, the stilling of the mind, heads the Vedāntic disciplines; She is that peace itself, and grants it.

meaning_check.note: 'and bliss' is not in the name; śama is tranquility.

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi of resemblance (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa)
samasa.vigraha: बन्धूकस्य कुसुमम् बन्धूककुसुमम्; बन्धूककुसुमस्य प्रख्या इव प्रख्या यस्याः सा बन्धूककुसुमप्रख्या
samasa.vigraha_iast: bandhūkasya kusumam bandhūkakusumam; bandhūkakusumasya prakhyā iva prakhyā yasyāḥ sā bandhūkakusumaprakhyā
samasa.explanation: (1) bandhūka-kusuma 'the bandhūka flower' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) prakhyā 'appearance, brightness' at the end of a compound means 'resembling': the whole is a bahuvrīhi, 'She whose radiance is like the bandhūka flower's'.

components.meaning: bandhūka, a shrub with bright red flowers (Pentapetes phoenicea)
appearance, radiance; (at the end of a compound) resembling

names.meaning: She whose radiance resembles the red bandhūka flower
names.significance: Her complexion is the red of dawn and of the bandhūka blossom, the color of compassion (anurāga) in Her dhyāna.

meaning_check.note: The comparison is of color and radiance; 'beauty and grace' is not in the name. 'bandhUka' put into IAST.

names.meaning: She who is Bālā, the ever-young girl
names.significance: In Śrīvidyā, Bālā Tripurasundarī is the Goddess as a girl, worshipped with the three-syllable Bālā mantra, often the first initiation; traditionally She never leaves the innocence and playfulness of a child.

meaning_check.note: 'never forsakes the nature of a child' is interpretation; the name itself is Bālā, 'the girl'.

samasa.explanation: vinodinī 'one who amuses herself, takes delight' is the head; līlā 'play' stands to it in the instrumental: 'She who delights Herself with play'.

names.meaning: She who delights in Her sport
names.significance: Creation, preservation and dissolution are Her play (līlā), undertaken not from need but from the fullness of delight; the name echoes Lalitā, 'She who plays'.

samasa.explanation: su 'good, well' qualifies maṅgala 'auspiciousness', and the whole describes Her: 'She whose auspiciousness is perfect'. The feminine is formed with -ī.

names.meaning: She who is eternally auspicious; She who is never widowed
names.significance: A sumaṅgalī is a married woman whose husband lives; since Her Lord Kāmeśvara is eternal, Her auspiciousness never ends.

samasa.explanation: -karī 'making' (√kṛ with the suffix -a, feminine -ī) is the head and takes sukha as its object: 'She who makes happiness'.

names.meaning: She who gives happiness
names.significance: She causes happiness in this world and the bliss of liberation beyond it.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: शोभनः वेषः सुवेषः; सुवेषेण आढ्या सुवेषाढ्या
samasa.vigraha_iast: śobhanaḥ veṣaḥ suveṣaḥ; suveṣeṇa āḍhyā suveṣāḍhyā
samasa.explanation: (1) su-veṣa 'beautiful attire' (prādi-tatpuruṣa). (2) āḍhyā 'rich, abounding' is the head and takes (1) in the instrumental: 'rich in beautiful attire'.

names.meaning: She who is rich in beautiful attire and adornment
names.significance: Her splendid dress and ornaments are the sign of the auspicious married state (names 967 and 970).

meaning_check.note: The sense is 'rich in fine attire'; 'very attractive' is interpretation.

names.previous_split_issues: veṣāḍhyā was left as one row ('rich in attire'); it is veṣa + āḍhyā, joined by savarṇa-dīrgha.

samasa.explanation: su 'well' + vāsinī 'dwelling' (√vas with -in): 'she who dwells well', the established word for a married woman whose husband is living.

names.meaning: She who is ever auspiciously married
names.significance: A suvāsinī lives in the auspicious married state; Her union with Kāmeśvara is eternal. The next name speaks of the worship of suvāsinīs.

sandhi.rule: yaṇ: ī → y before an unlike vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci)

samasa.vigraha: सुवासिनीनाम् अर्चनम् सुवासिन्यर्चनम्; सुवासिन्यर्चनेन प्रीता सुवासिन्यर्चनप्रीता
samasa.vigraha_iast: suvāsinīnām arcanam suvāsinyarcanam; suvāsinyarcanena prītā suvāsinyarcanaprītā
samasa.explanation: (1) suvāsinī-arcana 'the worship of suvāsinīs' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa; the genitive is read as objective: the suvāsinīs are honored). (2) prītā 'pleased' is the head and takes (1) in the instrumental of cause: 'pleased by the worship of suvāsinīs'. The genitive could also be subjective, 'worship performed by suvāsinīs'.

components.meaning: suvāsinī: a married woman whose husband is living

names.meaning: She who is pleased by the worship of suvāsinīs (auspicious married women)
names.significance: In Śrīvidyā practice suvāsinī-pūjā honors married women as living forms of the Goddess; She takes that honor as given to Herself.

meaning_check.note: The worship is traditionally the honoring of suvāsinīs (objective genitive); the old reading, worship performed by them, is kept as an alternative under uncertain.

names.previous_split_issues: suvāsiny was given in its sandhi form and glossed 'well-dressed/fragrant women'; the stem is suvāsinī, a married woman whose husband lives.
names.uncertain: suvāsinī-arcana may mean worship OF suvāsinīs (the Śrīvidyā rite of suvāsinī-pūjā) or worship BY them; the first is followed.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha across the name boundary: ā + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101); the doubled avagraha marks the absorbed long ā. Bhāskararāya reads the name as ā-śobhanā; the sounds would be the same if one cut prītā + śobhanā, so the division is his reading, not a sound change inside the name

samasa.explanation: The preposition ā 'all around, fully' qualifies śobhanā 'radiant, beautiful': 'radiant on every side, entirely beautiful'. Read without ā (śobhanā), the sense would be simply 'the beautiful one'.

names.meaning: She who is radiant through and through
names.significance: Her beauty has no flaw or side that is not radiant; it shines inwardly as purity of mind (name 973) as well as outwardly.

meaning_check.note: ā 'fully, on every side' rendered; 'always' was a loose gloss of it.

names.uncertain: The verse string can be cut prītā + āśobhanā or prītā + śobhanā with identical sound; Bhāskararāya's division (āśobhanā) is followed.

samasa.explanation: śuddha 'pure' qualifies mānasa 'mind', and the whole describes Her: 'She whose mind is pure'; mānasa takes the feminine -ā. Read as an instrumental bahuvrīhi (śuddhaṃ mānasaṃ yayā), it means 'She by whom the mind is purified'.

components.note: mānasa (from manas), with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She whose mind is pure; She who purifies the minds of Her worshipers
names.significance: Her own awareness is untouched by any impurity, and meditation on Her purifies the devotee's mind.

meaning_check.note: 'one who' made 'She who'.

sandhi.rule: the final m of the prefix sam becomes anusvāra and then the nasal of the following t-row, n (Pāṇini 8.3.23, 8.4.59)

samasa.vigraha: बिन्दौ तर्पणम् बिन्दुतर्पणम्; बिन्दुतर्पणेन सन्तुष्टा बिन्दुतर्पणसन्तुष्टा
samasa.vigraha_iast: bindau tarpaṇam bindutarpaṇam; bindutarpaṇena santuṣṭā bindutarpaṇasantuṣṭā
samasa.explanation: (1) bindu-tarpaṇa 'the libation offered at the bindu' (saptamī-tatpuruṣa). (2) santuṣṭā 'fully satisfied' is the head and takes (1) in the instrumental: 'satisfied by the libations at the bindu'.

components.meaning: the bindu, the central point of the Śrīcakra

components.note: sam + √tuṣ 'to be content', past participle, feminine

names.meaning: She who is pleased by the libations offered at the bindu of the Śrīcakra
names.significance: In Śrīcakra worship tarpaṇa is offered to Her at the central bindu; inwardly the bindu is in the sahasrāra, where the nectar of union satisfies Her.

meaning_check.note: 'shrIchakra' put into IAST; tarpaṇa rendered as libation.

samasa.explanation: -jā 'born' (√jan with the suffix -a) is the head; pūrva 'before, first' qualifies it adverbially: 'born first'.

names.meaning: She who is the first-born, preceding all
names.significance: Before the gods and the worlds came to be, She was; She is the primordial power from which all else is born.

meaning_check.note: Wording tidied ('ahead of everyone' made 'preceding all').

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner dvigu); or karmadhāraya
samasa.vigraha: त्रयाणाम् पुराणाम् समाहारः त्रिपुरम्; त्रिपुराणाम् अम्बिका त्रिपुराम्बिका; अथवा त्रिपुरा च असौ अम्बिका च त्रिपुराम्बिका
samasa.vigraha_iast: trayāṇām purāṇām samāhāraḥ tripuram; tripurāṇām ambikā tripurāmbikā; athavā tripurā ca asau ambikā ca tripurāmbikā
samasa.explanation: (1) tri-pura 'the three cities' (dvigu). (2) ambikā 'mother' is the head and the cities stand to it in the genitive: 'the Mother of the three cities'. As a karmadhāraya, Tripurā (the Goddess) and Ambikā are one: 'Tripurā the Mother' (then tripurā + ambikā, ā + a → ā).

names.meaning: She who is the Mother of the three cities (tripuras)
names.significance: Tripurāmbā is the presiding deity (cakreśvarī) of the eighth enclosure of the Śrīcakra, the inner triangle; the three cities are read as every triad: the three worlds, bodies, states and powers.

meaning_check.note: 'tripuras' put into IAST.

names.uncertain: Genitive ('Mother of the three cities') and appositional ('Tripurā the Mother') analyses are both current.

samasa.vigraha: दश मुद्राः दशमुद्राः; दशमुद्राभिः समाराध्या दशमुद्रासमाराध्या
samasa.vigraha_iast: daśa mudrāḥ daśamudrāḥ; daśamudrābhiḥ samārādhyā daśamudrāsamārādhyā
samasa.explanation: (1) daśa-mudrā 'the ten mudrās' (dvigu). (2) samārādhyā 'to be worshipped fully' is the head and takes (1) in the instrumental: 'to be worshipped with the ten mudrās'.

components.meaning: mudrā: ritual gesture, seal; also the goddess of that gesture

names.meaning: She who is worshipped with the ten mudrās
names.significance: The ten mudrās of Śrīcakra worship are Sarvasaṅkṣobhiṇī, Sarvavidrāviṇī, Sarvākarṣiṇī, Sarvavaśaṅkarī, Sarvonmādinī, Sarvamahāṅkuśā, Sarvakhecarī, Sarvabījā, Sarvayoni and Sarvatrikhaṇḍā; each is both a gesture and a goddess of an enclosure.

meaning_check.note: The ten mudrā names, given in ITRANS, moved to significance and put into IAST.

sandhi.rule: the m of vaśam becomes anusvāra and then the nasal of the following k-row, ṅ (Pāṇini 8.3.23, 8.4.59)

samasa.explanation: vaśaṅkarī 'one who brings under control' (vaśa + √kṛ, with the augment m that keeps vaśam's form, Pāṇini 6.3.67) is the head, and Tripurāśrī is the one brought under Her sway.

components.meaning: Tripurāśrī, presiding goddess of the fifth enclosure of the Śrīcakra

names.meaning: She who holds Tripurāśrī under Her sway
names.significance: Tripurāśrī is the cakreśvarī of the fifth enclosure (sarvārthasādhaka cakra); traditionally Tripurāśrī is also read as the fortune (śrī) of the three worlds, which She commands.

meaning_check.note: 'tripurAshrI' put into IAST.

names.previous_split_issues: Tripurāśrī was split into tripurā 'three cities' and śrī 'sacred'; it is one deity's name.
names.uncertain: Tripurāśrī as the fifth-enclosure deity and as 'the fortune of the three worlds' are both traditional readings.

samasa.explanation: mudrā 'gesture' is the head; jñāna stands to it in the genitive: 'the gesture of knowledge'.

names.meaning: She who is in the form of the jñāna mudrā
names.significance: In the jñāna (cin) mudrā the index finger, the individual self, bows to join the thumb, the supreme: She is the knowledge that gesture teaches.

meaning_check.note: 'j~nAna mudrA' put into IAST.

samasa.explanation: The gerundive gamyā 'to be reached' is the head and takes jñāna in the instrumental: 'to be reached through knowledge'.

names.meaning: She who is to be reached through knowledge
names.significance: Traditionally the knowledge is the realization of identity with Her, the path of jñāna.

meaning_check.note: 'the yoga of' is not in the name; jñāna is knowledge.

samasa.type: dvandva and karmadhāraya, completed by the possessive suffix -in
samasa.vigraha: ज्ञानम् च ज्ञेयम् च ज्ञानज्ञेये; ज्ञानज्ञेये एव स्वरूपम् ज्ञानज्ञेयस्वरूपम्; ज्ञानज्ञेयस्वरूपम् अस्याः अस्ति इति ज्ञानज्ञेयस्वरूपिणी
samasa.vigraha_iast: jñānam ca jñeyam ca jñānajñeye; jñānajñeye eva svarūpam jñānajñeyasvarūpam; jñānajñeyasvarūpam asyāḥ asti iti jñānajñeyasvarūpiṇī
samasa.explanation: (1) jñāna-jñeya 'knowledge and the knowable' (itaretara-dvandva). (2) That pair is identified with svarūpa 'own form, nature'. (3) The possessive -in (feminine -iṇī) makes the whole describe Her: 'She whose own nature is both knowledge and the known'.

components.meaning: what is to be known, the known

names.meaning: She who is both knowledge and the known
names.significance: In the non-dual view the knower, knowing and known are one consciousness; She is both the knowing and its object.

samasa.explanation: mudrā 'gesture' is the head; yoni 'source, womb' stands to it in the genitive: 'the gesture of the yoni'.

names.meaning: She who is in the form of the yoni mudrā
names.significance: The yoni mudrā is the ninth of the ten mudrās of Śrīcakra worship (Sarvayoni); it shows Her as the source of all.

meaning_check.note: 'yonimudrA' put into IAST.

sandhi.rule: guṇa: ā + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: त्रयः खण्डाः यस्याः सा त्रिखण्डा; त्रिखण्डायाः ईशी त्रिखण्डेशी
samasa.vigraha_iast: trayaḥ khaṇḍāḥ yasyāḥ sā trikhaṇḍā; trikhaṇḍāyāḥ īśī trikhaṇḍeśī
samasa.explanation: (1) tri-khaṇḍā 'that which has three parts', the name of the tenth mudrā (bahuvrīhi). (2) īśī 'sovereign lady' is the head and the mudrā stands to it in the genitive: 'the sovereign of the Trikhaṇḍā'.

components.note: khaṇḍa, feminine as the name of the mudrā

names.meaning: She who is the sovereign of the Trikhaṇḍā, the tenth mudrā
names.significance: Trikhaṇḍā (Sarvatrikhaṇḍā) is the tenth mudrā, used in invoking Her; traditionally the three parts are also the three kūṭas (sections) of the Pañcadaśī mantra, so She rules the mantra itself.

meaning_check.note: 'mudrA, the trikhaNDa' put into IAST.

names.previous_split_issues: khaṇḍeśī was left as one row; it is khaṇḍā + īśī, joined by guṇa.
names.uncertain: Trikhaṇḍā as the tenth mudrā, or the three kūṭas of the Pañcadaśī mantra: both are traditional.

samasa.explanation: tri 'three' qualifies guṇa 'quality', and the whole describes Her: 'She who has the three guṇas'; guṇa takes the feminine -ā.

components.note: guṇa, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She who is endowed with the three guṇas of sattva, rajas and tamas
names.significance: As Prakṛti She wields the three qualities in creating, sustaining and dissolving, though Herself beyond them (name 961). Her final ā absorbs the a of the next name, ambā.

meaning_check.note: 'guNas' put into IAST.

names.previous_split_issues: guṇā was glossed as plural 'qualities'; it is guṇa with the feminine ending of the bahuvrīhi.

names.meaning: She who is the Mother of all beings, the Mother of the universe
names.significance: The simplest of Her names, the child's word for mother; traditionally the triad triguṇā-ambā is read as the Mother who works through the three guṇas.

meaning_check.note: Capitalization tidied.

names.uncertain: triguṇāmbā can also be read as one word, 'the Mother of the three guṇas'; the 1,000-name count follows Bhāskararāya's two names.

samasa.vigraha: त्रयः कोणाः यस्य तत् त्रिकोणम्; त्रिकोणे गच्छति इति त्रिकोणगा
samasa.vigraha_iast: trayaḥ koṇāḥ yasya tat trikoṇam; trikoṇe gacchati iti trikoṇagā
samasa.explanation: (1) tri-koṇa 'that which has three angles', a triangle (bahuvrīhi). (2) -gā 'going, abiding' (√gam with the suffix -a) is the head and takes the triangle in the locative: 'She who abides in the triangle'.

names.meaning: She who resides in the triangle
names.significance: The inner triangle of the Śrīcakra surrounds the bindu and is Her seat (the eighth enclosure); inwardly it is the triangle in the mūlādhāra and the kāmakalā.
names.previous_split_issues: gā was glossed 'pervading'; it is 'going, abiding in'.

samasa.vigraha: न विद्यते अघम् यस्याः सा अनघा
samasa.vigraha_iast: na vidyate agham yasyāḥ sā anaghā
samasa.explanation: nañ 'not' with agha 'sin': 'She in whom there is no sin'. na becomes an- before a vowel; the members meet without further sound change.

agha, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She who is sinless
names.significance: No sin or impurity touches Her, and She removes the sins of those who remember Her.

samasa.explanation: adbhuta 'wondrous' qualifies cāritra 'conduct, deeds', and the whole describes Her: 'She whose deeds are wondrous'; cāritra takes the feminine -ā.

names.meaning: She whose deeds are marvelous
names.significance: Her deeds, from slaying Bhaṇḍa to granting liberation, surpass anything the mind can measure.

samasa.vigraha: वाञ्छिताः अर्थाः वाञ्छितार्थाः; वाञ्छितार्थान् प्रददाति इति वाञ्छितार्थप्रदायिनी
samasa.vigraha_iast: vāñchitāḥ arthāḥ vāñchitārthāḥ; vāñchitārthān pradadāti iti vāñchitārthapradāyinī
samasa.explanation: (1) vāñchita-artha 'desired objects' (karmadhāraya). (2) pradāyinī 'giver' is the head and takes (1) as its object: 'She who gives the desired objects'.

names.meaning: She who grants what is desired
names.significance: Traditionally She grants each worshiper what they seek, and in the end leads them to desire only Her.

verse_notes.note: Name 925 kaulinīkevalā is a single name (some printings write it as two words, which breaks the count); name 926 begins with an-arghya 'priceless', whose initial a is hidden in the long ā (avagraha). In 923 the long ā after the first dakṣiṇa hides the a- of a-dakṣiṇa: right-hand and left-hand worshipers.
Name 928 stutimatī is stuti + the possessive suffix -matī ('possessed of praise'), not mati 'mind'; 930 manasvinī and 931 mānavatī are likewise possessive derivatives.
Names 939 and 940 play on the same syllables and must be divided differently: param-odārā (parama + udārā) and parām-odā (para + āmodā).
Name 945 recalls the Vāmakeśvara Tantra, a root text of Śrīvidyā. From 946 a run of names begins on pañca 'five' (946–950).
The run on 'five' ends with 950 (the five offerings of worship); 951–952 then pair śāśvatī 'eternal' with śāśvataiśvaryā 'whose sovereignty is eternal'.

धराधरसुता is divided by Bhāskararāya into two names, dharā 'the Earth' (955) and dharasutā 'daughter of the mountain' (956); there is no sound change at the cut. Read as one word (dharādhara-sutā) it would be a single name and the count of 1,000 would fall short. Names 960–962 form a rising series on atītā 'gone beyond'.
The second half is a run of su- names (967–970), on auspicious married life; it leads into 971.

external_sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101); the doubled avagraha marks the absorbed long ā

verse_notes.note: Name 972 is āśobhanā (Bhāskararāya's division of prītā + āśobhanā); the sound would be the same with prītā + śobhanā, so the doubled avagraha records the reading. Name 976 Tripurāmbikā is the presiding deity of the eighth enclosure of the Śrīcakra.

Names 977–983 concern the ten mudrās of Śrīcakra worship and the deities of its enclosures: 978 Tripurāśrī presides over the fifth enclosure; 982 yonimudrā and 983 trikhaṇḍā (in the next śloka) are the ninth and tenth mudrās. Tripurāśrī is one deity's name: divide tripurāśrī-vaśaṅkarī.

savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101); the avagraha marks the absorbed a of adbhuta

report.summary: Checked all 67 names of ślokas 171–180 against text.json: sandhi at every member and prefix junction, a layered samāsa analysis with vigraha-vākyas in pausa form, and every meaning against that analysis. Bhāskararāya's divisions are explained where they fall (955 dharā / 956 dharasutā with no sound change; 972 āśobhanā and 985 ambā across savarṇa-dīrgha), and two misread members were corrected in the word tables: 923 is dakṣiṇa + a-dakṣiṇa (left-hand worshipers had been dropped) and 978 Tripurāśrī is one deity, not 'three cities' + 'sacred'. No meaning had to be replaced outright; most edits put ITRANS into IAST or removed words not in the name. No problem was found in the Sanskrit text.
